newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close lower on dollar, poll fears.
newsitem.headline: French shares close lower on dollar, poll fears.

text.p: French shares closed lower on Friday, ignoring rises on Wall Street and fresh records in London, because of a weaker dollar and unease over a diminishing lead of the government in pre-election opinion polls.

The French market was closed on Thursday when remarks by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan helped bonds and shares and it woke up to a dollar hurt by comments by Japan's "Mr Yen" Eisuke Sakakibara.
An IPSOS poll released on Thursday evening showed a close race between the centre-right and the opposition Socialist and Communist parties ahead of the May 25/June 1 election.
"It's starting to hot up. At the start everybody thought that the right would win, now there are some doubts," a broker said.
But analysts said the markets had not yet woken up to the possibility the left could win.
"It astonishes me that they (the market) do not seem to have into account that the left could win," Deutsche Bank economist Patrick Mange said.
Others said that the Socialsists, if they won power, would probably remain committed to European monetary union in any case.
The CAC-40 index closed down 0.36 percent at 2633.91 and May futures were 9.5 points lower at 2,616. Volume was 5.74 billion francs of which 4.3 billion in blue-chip shares.
"The market is digesting the fall of the dollar and the opinion polls which are not good (for the ruling majority)," a share dealer said.

Traders were reluctant about pronouncing themselves on the market's direction next week, just two weeks from the May 25 and June 1 two-round parliamentary election and a few days away from the May 20 meeting of the Federal Reserve policy council.

"There is too much uncertainty about where the market is going. It will very much depend on opinion polls and statements by the one and other in the election campaign," said a broker, adding a continuing U.S. bond rally could support share prices.

The CAC-40 stood at 2,522.67 when President Jacques Chirac called the early parliamentary election on April 21. It rose to a close of 2,651.93 on May 6 before slipping. The index lost 0.8 percent this week.

* Lagardere Groupe, up 3.07 percent at 181.40 francs, was boosted by the alliances with Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace and British Aerospace in its bid for the state's majority stake in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
CCF Elysees Bourse raised its recommendation to buy from accumulate.
Bernard Angeniol of CPR said that with the alliances Lagardere was better placed to win the bidding than Alcatel Alsthom, down 1.55 percent at 637 francs.
* Gaumont, up 5.20 percent at 465 francs, was the biggest riser, boosted by the opening day box office success of of the new Luc Besson movie "The Fifth Element".
* Dassault Aviation, in merger talks with Aerospatiale, was up 4.67 percent at 1,210 francs.
* Most active share was Danone, with one block trade for 376.000 shares at 874 francs each.
Total turnover in Danone was some 450 million francs, of which 330 million in the block trade which respresented 0.5 percent of the company's capital.
* Loss-leader was Plastic Omnium, down 3.76 percent at 486 francs.
